execution: GitHub Actions, Ubuntu runner, Python 3.11, CPU
data: Analytic synthetic heat-equation and generated graph data only; no patient, clinical or cohort data.

pinn.task: 2D Neumann heat equation with known analytic solution
pinn.interpretation: Improved substantially over the untrained initialization but retains about 9.1% held-out relative L2 error and a nonzero PDE residual; further tuning and independent benchmark cases are needed.

fno.task: 2D periodic heat semigroup with exact Fourier solution
fno.interpretation: Held-out error about 1.36%, substantially below the no-evolution persistence baseline on this synthetic operator.

gnn.task: Predict synthetic local immune-type neighbour fraction from generated spatial graph features
gnn.interpretation: Learns the synthetic graph statistic with lower held-out MSE than a constant-mean baseline; the target is generated from graph topology and is not a measured biological phenotype.

limitations: All tasks are analytic or synthetic; no breast-cancer molecular, pathology, imaging, treatment or outcome data were used.
Different architectures solve different mathematical tasks; their errors must not be compared as a model ranking.
The PINN benchmark retains non-negligible error and PDE residual.
The GNN predicts a graph-construction statistic by design; it does not infer tumour immune infiltration.
No biological validity, clinical performance, treatment-response prediction or patient-level utility is established.
